places.name: Alten Corimont
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §2 (Alten Corimont M4: captain of the port; smuggling, transit, salvage, the northern trunk; Hist: NONE)
lore: Lore:Alten Corimont; Lore:All Flags Navy

why.founding: A river port ESE of the Hatching Pools that grew into a small town by being institutionally neutral about cargo: it sits on the northern trunk between Stormhold and Thorn, on water deep enough for a laden hull and far enough from any customs regime that both of them use it.
why.siteAdvantages: The last reach of navigable river below the northern rim, with an oxbow that makes a natural basin, firm banks for warehousing and a rim road behind it that crosses to Morrowind without passing a post.
why.occupantsMotive: A captain of the port whose only law is a nailed-up price list, freeholder crews with no tribe and no tree, Dunmer factors from the Morrowind trade and Nord hands off the northern hulls.
why.pressures: There is no Hist here — the register is explicit — so nothing binds anyone to anything except the list; Stormhold's vicecanons would like the trade and cannot reach it; Rockpoint downriver still resents losing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either Stormhold or Thorn made the port lawful, its whole reason to exist is gone; if the river silted below the oxbow, the town is a village in five years.

hardConstraints: navigable water for a laden hull
sheltered basin off the legal lanes
no Hist within the settlement — canon
preferences: an oxbow or confluence basin
deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes
a rim road behind it that avoids every post

occupants: one D3 captain of the port who counts rather than fights

vibe.silhouette: a beached hull sitting upright among the houses, too big for the street it ends, and warehouse gables behind it
vibe.palette: weathered grey timber everywhere, tar black, and cargo colours that do not belong together — Dunmer lacquer, Nord paint, Imperial red
vibe.materials: the town is built out of other people's cargo: crate timber, ship planking, salvaged spars, with mud render only where nothing else was to hand
vibe.signatureFeature: a price list nailed up in public that names contraband by grade, and is therefore the most complete economic document in the province
vibe.mood: transactional, unbothered, dangerous only if you are slow
vibe.approach: the hull's shape resolves out of the roofline from upriver, long before you can read the town
vibe.senses: hulls working against the bank, four languages, tar, wet rope, cooking from three cuisines at once

places.complexityJustification: The zone's only M4 and its whole organising institution: a price list, a port captain, a beached hull hall and a two-culture waterfront. Districts and a service economy, but no scripting beyond Morrowind level.

places.namingRule: named for the road it stages
sources: lore: Lore:Argonian (bones brought to the dirt); Blackrose Chainbreakers (quest plan)

why.founding: Carriers walking south with the dead need a stage a day out from the carrying house.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm dry ground on the southbound road, a day's walk from the house.
why.occupantsMotive: Two or three carriers and their loads, resting.
why.pressures: Nobody else will camp within sight of them, which suits everyone.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the road were rerouted, the stage moves with it — the site means nothing, the spacing means everything.

hardConstraints: a day's walk from the waystation
preferences: off the road, out of sight of other camps

vibe.silhouette: a small camp with its loads racked, not stacked
vibe.palette: grey cloth, small fire
vibe.materials: carrying frames, wrapping cloth, one fire
vibe.signatureFeature: the bundles are racked off the ground on frames before anybody sits down
vibe.approach: you see the frames first and understand
vibe.senses: one low conversation; a fire

places.name: The Carrying House
sources: uesp:Lore:Argonian (the dead must be brought to the dirt)
lore: Lore:Argonian (bones brought to the dirt redeem a death away from the Hist); White Rose Prison

why.founding: Argonians who die away from a Hist can still return if their bones are brought to the dirt — and this zone has no Hist at all, so every death here starts a journey south.
why.siteAdvantages: On the trunk route at the point where the southbound road and the river both leave the freeholds.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers who take the dead of a town that cannot bury them, for a fee they are ashamed of.
why.pressures: The house is always full, because the freeholds produce more Hist-less dead than any comparable ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Hist were ever planted at the free port, this house closes and the carriers lose a trade.

preferences: at the zone's southern threshold

vibe.silhouette: a long low house with racked bundles under its eaves
vibe.palette: bleached bone, wrapped grey cloth, dark timber
vibe.materials: timber racks, wrapping cloth, carrying frames
vibe.signatureFeature: racks of wrapped bundles labelled with destinations two weeks' travel south
vibe.mood: the zone's one act of tenderness
vibe.approach: you smell the resin used for wrapping before you reach it
vibe.senses: cloth; and a great deal of silence

places.name: The Hard
sources: world/sources/lore/topics/material-culture.md (Argonians crew foreign hulls, build small craft)
lore: Lore:Sea Transportation; material-culture (Argonians crew foreign hulls, build small craft)

why.founding: Foreign keeled hulls come this far up the river and have to be laid over and scraped somewhere the owner is not watching.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm shelving bank inside the basin, with a hard bottom that will take a hull's weight at low water.
why.occupantsMotive: Boatwrights who build canoes beautifully and repair Nord hulls badly, on purpose, for money.
why.pressures: Hull identities change here: a name is planed off and another painted on, and everybody knows the going rate.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port were ever inspected, the hard is the first thing that would have to disappear.

preferences: inside the basin, out of the main channel

vibe.silhouette: a keeled hull lying over on its side on a mud bank, out of the water
vibe.palette: tar black, raw plank gold, river brown
vibe.materials: hull timber, steaming pit, paint pots
vibe.signatureFeature: a stack of planed-off nameboards under a bench, kept because someone thinks they might be needed again
vibe.approach: the laid-over hull reads as a building until it moves
vibe.senses: scraping; hot pitch; hammering that stops when strangers arrive

places.name: Chasecreek
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §4 (Chasecreek, NE of Alten Corimont: creek-mouth fishing hamlet and smuggler's lay-by)

why.founding: A fishing hamlet on the one dry rise at a creek mouth, which discovered that a boat can wait here unseen while the free port is being watched, and has lived off that ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A single flood-high rise with a creek deep enough to hide a hull and shallow enough that nobody follows.
why.occupantsMotive: Fisher households who are also, on about four nights a month, a lay-by with a fee.
why.pressures: The lay-by trade is worth more than the fish and everyone under sixteen already knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port's list ever covered waiting time, Chasecreek loses its niche and becomes a fishing hamlet again.

hardConstraints: a dry rise that never floods
a creek mouth deep enough to lie in
preferences: a night's row from the free port
no line of sight from the trunk route

vibe.silhouette: a dozen roofs on a single low rise with nothing else above water for a kilometre
vibe.palette: reed gold, mud grey, and one very good bought lamp per household
vibe.materials: mud render and reed on a rise, plus a great deal of unexplained plank
vibe.signatureFeature: every household has one expensive object that does not match anything else it owns
vibe.approach: the rise is the only thing above the reed for a long way
vibe.senses: reed, frogs, and a boat arriving at the wrong hour

places.name: The Bad Stack
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (the rim carries the province's relief)
docs/world/00-core.md (acceptance rule: large logical surfaces climbable by default)

why.founding: A rotten limestone stack on the border rim beside the smugglers' traverse, which is the only reason anyone is ever near it.
why.siteAdvantages: It shortcuts a day off the rim crossing for anyone willing to climb it, and it is visible from most of the high ground on this side.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. A freehold courier's kit is still on the second ledge with the rope cut above it.
why.pressures: The traverse below it is used weekly and the fan reaches the path; two of the four fixed lines have gone.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it takes the traverse with it, the rim crossing moves twenty kilometres and the freeholds lose their quiet door into Morrowind.

hardConstraints: standing rock above a used route
a debris fan reaching the path
preferences: landforms: summit, cliff-bench, ridge-end
water relation: none
a summit cache above the traverse

vibe.silhouette: a fissured stack above a switchback path, with a fan of scree fingering across the route
vibe.palette: grey rim rock, orange lichen, weathered rope
vibe.materials: rotten limestone, cut fixed lines, nothing built to last
vibe.signatureFeature: Four rope anchors driven at four different dates, two of them hanging with nothing on the end.
vibe.condition: failing on a schedule nobody has written down
vibe.mood: a shortcut that has stopped being one
vibe.approach: The scree on the path tells you before the stack does.
vibe.senses: loose stone underfoot, wind through the fissures, rope slapping rock

places.name: The Broken Bond
sources: lore: guilds-and-orders dossier (the EEC is gone; its wharves and bonded stores are not)

why.founding: The Company built a bonded store on the northern river when the trade was lawful; the free port opened it the year the charter died and has used it ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: The only cargo-bearing stone building in the zone, on the basin's firm bank.
why.occupantsMotive: The port captain's men, who store bonded goods in a store that is no longer bonded and find that funny.
why.pressures: The seals were cut, not forged, and the Company's manifest is still nailed inside naming a dead consignee.
why.wouldChangeIf: If an Imperial claim were ever pressed, the free port's entire warehousing is legally stolen.

preferences: attached to the free port
a wharf within 300 m

vibe.silhouette: a stone cargo hall among timber sheds, obviously built by someone else
vibe.palette: Company red gone pink, grey stone, cargo colours
vibe.materials: Imperial ashlar with freehold timber lean-tos bolted to it
vibe.signatureFeature: a Company seal cut clean through with a saw, and the sawn halves kept nailed either side of the door as a joke
vibe.condition: sound, over-used, extended in every direction
vibe.approach: the one stone gable in a timber town
vibe.senses: cargo being moved at hours cargo should not be moved

places.name: The Standing Slate
sources: lore: Lore:Shells and Stones; material-culture (daril); labour-and-bondage dossier (debt becomes owing)

why.founding: In a town whose only law is a price list, the house that runs Shells and Stones is effectively the bank, and the debt slate is effectively the law.
why.siteAdvantages: In the free port's densest street, one door from the hull hall.
why.occupantsMotive: A house crew who buy debts and sell them on to the hiring yard.
why.pressures: Half the freeholders in town owe the slate, which is why the captain of the port is careful with it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If someone burned the slate, this zone's whole informal credit system goes with it — and so does the hiring yard.

preferences: one door from the town's social hall

vibe.silhouette: a low doorway with no sign and more light than any window near it
vibe.palette: lamp red, chalk white, dark timber
vibe.materials: crate-timber walls, one very good table, hung lamps
vibe.signatureFeature: a debt slate the height of a wall, chalked and re-chalked, that is the nearest thing this zone has to a legal record
vibe.condition: worn, expensive in the places that matter
vibe.mood: the town's real seat of power
vibe.approach: you hear the dice from the street
vibe.senses: dice on wood; chalk; someone being told a number

places.name: The Last Deep
sources: lore: region grammar: deep river corridor; Lore:Sea Transportation (small-draft craft are the province's freight)

why.founding: Above the free port the river shallows to a channel a laden hull cannot use, so cargo transfers to poled craft here — and the limit moves every season.
why.siteAdvantages: A confluence at -6.5 m relative depth where three channels meet and the deep water ends.
why.occupantsMotive: Transfer crews and a board-keeper whose season line is the district's most argued-about number.
why.pressures: In a dry year the limit drops two kilometres and half the district's freight costs change.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a dredge were ever run, the free port could take hulls upriver and Alten Corimont's monopoly on transfer ends.

hardConstraints: landings both sides of the limit
preferences: at a confluence
a porter relay on the land route

vibe.silhouette: far more small craft than the shore behind them explains
vibe.palette: river brown, pole-timber pale, cargo canvas grey
vibe.materials: transfer stages, poled craft, stacked cargo
vibe.signatureFeature: a navigable-limit board with this season's line and last season's still legible below it
vibe.mood: commercial argument as a way of life
vibe.approach: the boats thin out to nothing above it
vibe.senses: poles in gravel; disputes about draught

places.name: The Hiring Yard
sources: docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (The Owing — owed-labour gangs, ledger offices, hiring halls)
lore: labour-and-bondage dossier (owings extendable, transferable, heritable in fact)

why.founding: Debts bought at the gambling house become owings, and owings become gangs — the yard is where the people who lost their ground wait to be told where they are working.
why.siteAdvantages: A hard standing beside the porter yard, on the only road out of the free port.
why.occupantsMotive: Households whose owing was called in, and a broker's clerk with a ledger.
why.pressures: Nobody here is chained and nobody here can leave, and the difference is legally important and practically nil.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Chainbreaker cell reached the yard, the free port's labour supply stops on the same day.

hardConstraints: on the road out of a settlement
a hard standing and a ledger office
preferences: beside the freight yard it supplies

vibe.silhouette: a line of shelters along a fence with a single roofed office at one end
vibe.palette: grey canvas, mud, one painted door on the office
vibe.materials: salvaged canvas and crate timber; one proper building
vibe.signatureFeature: an office with a ledger in it that is the only writing anybody in this zone treats as binding
vibe.condition: permanent, in a form that pretends to be temporary
vibe.approach: the road out of town runs straight through it
vibe.senses: a ledger being read aloud; no reply

places.name: No-Tree
sources: lore: Lore:Lukiul; League of Open Water (quest plan); Lore:Hist

why.founding: The register is explicit that the free port has no Hist, and that is not an omission — it is the reason the freeholds exist. Everyone here is Hist-less by choice or by accident, and the camp on the town's edge is where that is admitted out loud.
why.siteAdvantages: The town's landward fringe, on ground the port does not administer.
why.occupantsMotive: Argonians with no tree to return to, plus outsiders who find that easier to be around.
why.pressures: The tribal villages upriver will not visit; Hissmir's reconnection rite is a two-week journey and a hard conversation.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Hist cutting were successfully planted here, the free port stops being a freehold and starts being a town.

preferences: on the landward fringe of the free port

vibe.silhouette: a village with a swept empty circle where a tree should be
vibe.palette: mud grey, undyed cloth, no amber anywhere
vibe.materials: mud render, crate timber, no ritual totems at all
vibe.signatureFeature: a planting circle dug, edged and kept swept for sixty years, with nothing in it
vibe.approach: the gap in the middle is visible before anything else
vibe.senses: no chimes; the province's characteristic sound simply missing

places.name: The Quay Room
sources: lore: Morrowind's corner club / tradehouse pattern (morrowind-content-density.md); Lore:Hissmir Fish-Eye Rye

why.founding: A port whose social hall is a beached hull still needs somewhere you can pay for a bed and a locked door.
why.siteAdvantages: On the basin front, one door from the hull hall and two from the gambling house.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who sells beds and rents silence.
why.pressures: Four languages in one room, and the guest book is worth more than the takings.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port were made lawful, the guest book becomes evidence and the keeper burns it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a mooring
preferences: inside the free port
a private room with its own stair

vibe.silhouette: a lit doorway with a mooring outside and a stable behind
vibe.palette: lamp yellow, tar black, cargo-crate walls
vibe.materials: crate timber and ship plank, one bought Imperial door
vibe.signatureFeature: a guest book kept in four scripts, none of them Jel, and a private stair that avoids the main room
vibe.approach: the noise reaches the basin
vibe.senses: four languages; cooking; a lock being turned upstairs

places.name: The Old Pens
sources: lore: Lore:House Dres; Lore:Archein; labour-and-bondage dossier (slavery ended; only the apparatus remains)

why.founding: House Dres took Argonians out of this river country for centuries, and the pens they used to hold and count them are still standing on the bank they loaded from.
why.siteAdvantages: A river landing with hard standing, sited for loading rather than living.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The free port will not use the ground and will not explain why to outsiders.
why.pressures: It is the one thing in this zone nobody makes a joke about.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Dunmer factors in town were ever formally associated with it, the freehold's trade with Morrowind ends overnight.

hardConstraints: a river landing built for loading
preferences: upstream of the free port
within sight of the trunk route

vibe.silhouette: stone pens and a loading ramp on an empty bank
vibe.palette: grey stone, rust, and nothing growing on the standing
vibe.materials: Dunmer-cut stone, iron rings, a ramp graded for people
vibe.signatureFeature: a loading ramp graded and railed for people rather than cargo, with the count-marks still cut into the gatepost
vibe.condition: sound; deliberately not repaired and deliberately not demolished
vibe.approach: the trunk road passes it and nobody looks
vibe.senses: nothing lives here — literally, not even birds

places.namingRule: named for the House remnant that founded it
sources: lore: Lore:House Dres; Lore:Tear; Lore:Red Year (4E 5); foreign-powers dossier (the cold settled frontier)

why.founding: A House holding left over from the Dres trade, now a Dunmer village on the wrong side of the border that stayed because going home was worse.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible upland shelf on the pass road, with its own water and a walled core.
why.occupantsMotive: Dunmer families three centuries settled, who factor for the free port and are not liked for it.
why.pressures: They are the largest concentration of the zone's 22% Dunmer minority and they live beside the pens their ancestors filled.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Morrowind reasserted a claim here, the free port's northern trade becomes a diplomatic asset instead of a crime.

preferences: distinct Velothi building grammar, never blended with the Argonian kit

vibe.silhouette: a walled core with organic Velothi roof shapes, unmistakably foreign on this skyline
vibe.palette: ash grey, lacquer red, black
vibe.materials: Velothi render and stone, imported roof tile, a wall
vibe.signatureFeature: an ancestor hall maintained for three hundred years by people who have never seen Morrowind
vibe.mood: proud, defensive, well aware of what is on the riverbank
vibe.approach: the roof shapes read wrong from a long way off
vibe.senses: a different language; a bell rather than a chime

places.namingRule: named for the levee it depends on
sources: lore: Lore:Saltrice; Lore:House Dres; Lore:Hereguard Plantation

why.founding: The seasonal floodplain below the freeholds is the only ground in the zone that grows a surplus, and the free port eats it.
why.siteAdvantages: Bunded flats on the floodplain where the river's annual rise can be let in and held.
why.occupantsMotive: Households who grow for the port's price list and are always slightly in its debt.
why.pressures: The levee is maintained collectively and one household always does less.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the levee failed in a bad year, the free port would be buying grain from Morrowind through its own smugglers.

preferences: within a day's haul of the free port

vibe.silhouette: flat bunded rectangles with a levee line above them
vibe.palette: water-sky silver, young green, levee ochre
vibe.materials: earth bunds, sluice boards, a levee walk
vibe.signatureFeature: a levee walk with each household's section marked, and one section visibly thinner
vibe.approach: the geometry is visible from the road above
vibe.senses: water moving through sluices; frogs; wind over flat crop

places.namingRule: named for the year cut into the largest cairn
sources: lore: Lore:Kothringi (cairn burial, glass beads); Lore:Knahaten Flu

why.founding: The people who died in the Flu here were not Argonian and had no Hist to go to, so they were cairned where they fell, by whoever was left.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm dry ground above the village, with loose stone to hand.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the cairns are re-stacked by passing travellers, which is a custom nobody can explain.
why.pressures: It is the largest visible evidence in the zone that a whole people used to live here.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a scholar counted them properly, the district's population history changes.

preferences: overlooking the ruin it belongs to

vibe.silhouette: hundreds of small stone piles across an open slope
vibe.palette: grey stone, brown grass, wide sky
vibe.materials: field stone, nothing worked, no markers
vibe.signatureFeature: hundreds of cairns and exactly one with a date cut into it
vibe.condition: re-stacked by strangers for six hundred years
vibe.approach: the slope reads as scree until the pattern resolves
vibe.senses: wind; stones being replaced by someone ahead of you

places.namingRule: named by its founders for the day they left
sources: lore: labour-and-bondage dossier; Blackrose Chainbreakers (quest plan)

why.founding: People whose owing was discharged, escaped or simply abandoned have nowhere to go back to, so they built somewhere.
why.siteAdvantages: Ground upstream that no syndicate has claimed, defensible enough to discourage a broker's men.
why.occupantsMotive: Ex-owed households running the place by open meeting, with a rule against ledgers.
why.pressures: The hiring yard's brokers want them back and the free port will not intervene either way.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the yard's ledger were destroyed, this shelter doubles in a season and becomes a settlement.

preferences: upstream of the hiring yard
no written records kept

vibe.silhouette: a compound with one gate and a lot of new timber
vibe.palette: raw timber, undyed cloth, cooking smoke
vibe.materials: green timber, salvaged crate wood, a thorn stockade
vibe.signatureFeature: a fire pit with a meeting circle around it, and no ledger, board or tally anywhere in the compound
vibe.approach: you are challenged before you arrive
vibe.senses: a lot of people talking at once, by design

places.namingRule: named for the stage it terminates
sources: lore: Lore:Jel (an oral language with no past or future tense); build-out: this is the letter/rumour delivery spine

why.founding: Word moves this zone by memorised message, and in a port that trades in information the relay is the most valuable post on the trunk.
why.siteAdvantages: On the trunk at a runner's stage from its neighbours, with a bench and a landing.
why.occupantsMotive: Runners who are paid twice for some messages and know which ones.
why.pressures: A message in transit is worth knowing and taking one is the zone's only crime that is punished.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the relay were bought outright by the port, the freeholds lose their only independent channel.

preferences: on the trunk
a departure board of carved tokens

vibe.palette: bleached timber, dark token wood
vibe.materials: carved tokens, a bench, a covered rest board

vibe.senses: one runner arriving out of breath, then leaving

places.name: The Open Ground
sources: lore: module 92 (three currency tiers: septims, barter, obligation); Lore:Argonian (barter economy); Lore:Lizard-Steed

why.founding: The price list has to be applied somewhere, and the stall row under the list board is where the zone's economy actually happens.
why.siteAdvantages: Level ground below the list board, one street from the basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Traders working in septims, Dunmer coin, barter and obligation at adjacent stalls.
why.pressures: The board is a public document that names contraband, which makes it the province's best commercial intelligence.

places.namingRule: named for the stretch of road they hold

sources: lore: fauna-hazards dossier (swamp rot, blood rot, greenspore); Lore:Knahaten Flu

places.name: The Anomaly
sources: lore: material-culture (metal use almost unheard of post-Duskfall)

why.founding: Everything that goes above the gorge has to come out of the water and go back in, and the men who drag it charge.
why.siteAdvantages: The one bank with a gradient a hauling gang can work, immediately below the narrows.
why.occupantsMotive: Six haulers with a charge board and a monopoly.
why.pressures: Cargo waits at both ends and is occasionally taxed twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a second slip were cut, the price halves — which is why it never is.

preferences: a mandatory node on the river route
the narrows 200-300 m off

vibe.silhouette: a greased timber ramp out of the water beside white water
vibe.palette: grease black, gold timber, spray
vibe.materials: rollers, hauling lines, a charge board
vibe.signatureFeature: a charge board with two prices on it: one for members of the port list, one for everyone else
vibe.approach: the slip is the first built thing you see
vibe.senses: rollers; straining rope; the narrows underneath

places.name: The Grinder
sources: lore: region grammar: deep river corridor; Lore:Seafalls; the arterial class needs its own hazards

why.founding: A gorge reach that cannot be run, and a logjam in it that has built itself into a crossable structure out of dead trees.
why.siteAdvantages: A gorge pinch in firm lowland where every flood's timber collects against the same rock.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it; four people are usually working the jam for salvage.
why.pressures: The jam is unstable, walkable, and the only dry crossing for two kilometres.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a flood cleared it, both the crossing and the salvage go in one night.

preferences: a logjam that is a walkable, climbable structure
a portage upstream

vibe.silhouette: a mass of bleached dead timber wedged across a gorge, with white water under it
vibe.palette: bone-white timber, black wet rock, brown-white water
vibe.materials: dead trees, wedged cargo, no built thing at all
vibe.signatureFeature: a bridge made entirely of drowned trees, that nobody built and everybody uses
vibe.approach: the sound reaches you from upstream first
vibe.senses: continuous roar; timber shifting under weight

places.namingRule: named for the river bend it stands on
sources: lore: Lore:Kothringi (silver-skinned, wiped out by the Knahaten Flu 2E 560); Lore:Knahaten Flu

why.founding: The Kothringi held river country like this and the Knahaten Flu ended them in 2E 560; their village on the bend was never reoccupied because nobody would.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bend site with a landing — the same reasons a village would be built there today.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The free port's crews will not tie up here and will not say it is superstition.
why.pressures: It is the best unoccupied river frontage in the zone and it has been empty for six hundred years.
why.wouldChangeIf: If somebody built here and did not die, the whole taboo collapses and the zone gains a settlement site.

hardConstraints: a river bend with a landing
preferences: visibly good ground that nobody uses

vibe.silhouette: house platforms and a landing on a good bend, with nothing standing on them
vibe.palette: grey stone footings, long grass, brown river
vibe.materials: stone footings and post holes — a people who built differently from Argonians
vibe.signatureFeature: a village-shaped clearing on the best ground for kilometres, with a two-hundred-year-old tree growing in the middle of the square
vibe.mood: the plague, still legible as an absence
vibe.approach: you notice the good ground before you notice why it is empty
vibe.senses: river; nothing else; the crews go quiet passing it

places.name: The Drawdown
sources: docs/world/50-hydrology.md (seasonal water levels as world state)
lore: region grammar: lake & standing water; module 50 (seasonal water levels are authored world state)

why.founding: The lake behind the freeholds drops four metres in the dry season and exposes a flat of deep soft mud that has swallowed people and things.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow lake shelf with a very large seasonal range.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing; scavengers work its edges when it is exposed.
why.pressures: What the drawdown reveals is worth having and the mud that reveals it will not let you stand.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the lake level were stabilised, everything down there stays down there.

preferences: a season-gated reward

vibe.silhouette: in the dry season, a cracked grey plain where a lake was
vibe.palette: grey mud, salt crust, bleached wood
vibe.materials: mud, exposed wreckage, stranded posts
vibe.signatureFeature: boats, posts and at least one cart standing upright in mud, exactly where they went down
vibe.condition: seasonal; six months of the year it does not exist
vibe.approach: you arrive in the wrong season and find water
vibe.senses: cracking mud; nothing living

places.namingRule: named for the village it was drawn around
sources: lore: Lore:Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603, wiped out the Kothringi, Lilmothiit and Horwalli)

why.founding: Somebody drew a line around the infected ground and marked it, and the marks were maintained long after the reason ended.
why.siteAdvantages: Along the natural boundary of a ridge and a stream, the easiest line to hold.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The marks are re-cut by the villages either side, out of habit.
why.pressures: The line is on nobody's map and is respected absolutely by everybody local.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were formally lifted, two villages would have to agree where the boundary now is.

preferences: between a ruin and a living village

vibe.silhouette: a line of cut marks on trees and posts, running dead straight over a ridge
vibe.palette: raw cut wood, weathered grey, green
vibe.materials: blazed trees, cut posts, one painted stone at each end
vibe.signatureFeature: blaze marks re-cut annually on trees that were saplings when the line was drawn
vibe.approach: you cross it without noticing, then find the next mark
vibe.senses: nothing; but locals stop talking at it

places.namingRule: named for the hermit's trade before they stopped
sources: lore: openworld research §3.2 (hermit: approach cost is the gate; the reward is knowledge, not loot)

why.founding: A ravine with no path, and one person at the bottom of it who used to keep the port's ledger and cannot any more.
why.siteAdvantages: Deliberately awkward: a box canyon with a spring and one climb in.
why.occupantsMotive: One person, and forty years of the free port's transactions written from memory on the walls.
why.pressures: They will trade what they remember for a specific favour and not for money, which in this zone is a statement.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the wall were read by the port, half the freeholds would be exposed.

preferences: deliberately far from the free port

vibe.silhouette: a thin smoke line out of a slot in the ground
vibe.palette: rock grey, one fire, green at the bottom
vibe.materials: a hut of ravine timber and stacked stone
vibe.signatureFeature: forty years of the port's ledger written on the ravine wall in charcoal, from memory
vibe.mood: the reward is a conversation and it is worth more than loot
vibe.approach: there is no route down; you find one
vibe.senses: water; one voice that has not been used in weeks

places.namingRule: named for its cargo, from the lot book
sources: docs/world/00-core.md acceptance rule: underwater POIs throughout appropriate regions
lore: openworld research §3.2 (wreck geometry IS the level; tier by depth and lock)

why.founding: A laden river hull that failed to hold the line above the bar and went down in the deep of the confluence.
why.siteAdvantages: It lies in the confluence hole at -6.5 m, out of the current but under a lot of water.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing; the salvage yard has stripped everything above the silt line.
why.pressures: The hold is under silt and the yard has decided it is not worth the drowning.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the river dropped in a hard dry season, the hold would be reachable and the yard would work it in a week.

preferences: in a confluence hole below a whitewater reach

vibe.silhouette: nothing above water; a shadow at the confluence
vibe.palette: tea-brown water, black timber, silver silt
vibe.materials: hull timber, silt, trapped cargo
vibe.signatureFeature: cargo still lashed in the hold under a metre of silt, in water too dark to work
vibe.approach: found by diving where the salvagers will not
vibe.senses: current noise above; nothing below

places.namingRule: named for the outfit holding it, not the legion that built it
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §6 (Fort Swampmoth model: held, but not by the Empire)
lore: module 20 §11 (the six-stage foreign-infrastructure life cycle)

why.founding: An intact Imperial fort on the trunk road, abandoned two hundred years ago, into which somebody moved and started charging.
why.siteAdvantages: It commands the trunk where the road cannot go around it — which is why the Legion built there.
why.occupantsMotive: A toll-taking outfit with a claim, a garrison of thirty and no legal standing whatsoever.
why.pressures: They are the free port's only rival for the road trade, and the port would rather they existed than the state did.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the state ever garrisoned it properly, the whole zone's economy is enclosed in a season.

preferences: the road cannot bypass it

occupants: D3 toll-takers and a hired garrison

vibe.silhouette: a square Imperial curtain wall with the wrong banners on it
vibe.palette: grey ashlar, faded eagle red, new banner colours
vibe.materials: Imperial ashlar with freehold timber additions bolted through the parapets
vibe.signatureFeature: an Imperial eagle still over the gate because nobody bothered to chisel it off, under a banner nobody can identify
vibe.approach: the walls are the only such shape in the zone and read from far off
vibe.senses: a gate being worked; drilling that is not quite drill

places.namingRule: named for the legion cohort that built it
sources: lore: argonia-4e201-state (occasional patrols; every 4E 201 data point is about withdrawal)

why.founding: The Empire posted a watch on the northern crossing; it was thinned at the Oblivion Crisis and never restored.
why.siteAdvantages: On the pass road below the saddle, sited to see the approach it no longer watches.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The pass keeper stores fuel in it.
why.pressures: It is the state's claim to the border, standing empty, four hundred metres from the smuggling route.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were re-manned, the ledges move a valley east within a month.

preferences: within sight of a route it does not control

vibe.silhouette: a small square post with an empty flagstaff
vibe.palette: grey stone, rust, faded eagle red
vibe.materials: Imperial dressed stone, a rotted timber gate
vibe.signatureFeature: an Imperial eagle over the door that nobody bothered to chisel off
vibe.condition: roofless in one bay, otherwise sound
vibe.approach: it is the first built thing on the pass and it is empty
vibe.senses: wind through empty embrasures

places.namingRule: named for the ridge it signals from
sources: lore: Lore:Jel (an oral language with no past or future tense); build-out: this is the letter/rumour delivery spine

why.founding: The rim route is too long and too exposed for a runner to hold the line, so the last stage signals by chime from a ridge end.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge end at 215 m with a clear line down to the porter yard.
why.occupantsMotive: One keeper who lives up there for a week at a time.
why.pressures: The chimes are audible to the pass station, which is the point of the argument about them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pass were manned, the chime line would be the first thing suppressed.

hardConstraints: a clear acoustic line to its neighbour
preferences: above the porter yard
audible from the pass

vibe.silhouette: a chime frame on a bare spur nose, silhouetted
vibe.palette: rock grey, bone chimes, sky
vibe.materials: a frame, hung bone and metal chimes, a one-man shelter
vibe.signatureFeature: a chime frame on a ridge that can be heard by the customs post it is warning people about
vibe.approach: the frame is one of the few skyline shapes in the zone
vibe.senses: chimes carrying a long way; wind

places.namingRule: named for the seam
sources: lore: Lore:Stormhold (crystals); Lore:Silyanorn; prisons dossier (Warden Varus's Tunnel Rats)

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal trade runs on seams in this rim country, and the ones outside the vicecanons' reach are cut by whoever gets there first.
why.siteAdvantages: An open cut on an upland spur where the seam breaks the surface.
why.occupantsMotive: Prospector gangs working without a licence, in shifts, watching the pass road.
why.pressures: The crystal moves through the free port because it cannot move through Stormhold.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the vicecanons enforced the licence here, the free port's most valuable cargo disappears.

preferences: off the licensed ground
within a day of the free port

vibe.silhouette: a raw white scar on a green hillside, visible for kilometres
vibe.palette: spoil white, hill green, tool rust
vibe.materials: cut rock, timber props, spoil heaps
vibe.signatureFeature: the spoil heap is visible from the pass road, and nobody up there has ever reported it
vibe.approach: the scar is one of the few things in the zone that reads at range
vibe.senses: picks; falling spoil; a lookout whistling

places.namingRule: named for the pass it sits below
sources: lore: Lore:Argonian (a comer cannot be refused); pacing: a hostile province needs a safety floor outside its cities

why.founding: The last fire below the pass, kept because people come down off the rim in a state.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest ground on the pass road that still has fuel within reach.
why.occupantsMotive: A household who have pulled more people off that mountain than the pass station has.
why.pressures: They know exactly what everyone who comes down is carrying and have never once said.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pass closed permanently, this house would have no reason to be here.

preferences: below the snowline
the last fire before the climb

vibe.silhouette: a fire visible from high on the pass road, and nothing else
vibe.palette: fire orange, grey rock, black slope
vibe.materials: dry stone, thatch weighted with rocks, one hearth
vibe.signatureFeature: a rack of dry clothes always hanging, for people who have not arrived yet
vibe.approach: you see it from above, which is unusual here
vibe.senses: fire; wind at the door; someone coughing

places.namingRule: named for the number of keystone sockets in it
sources: lore: Lore:Ayleid Wells; quest-provision keystone pattern (§13 typed provisions)

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids left keystone mechanisms across the fringe of this country, and one of them is cut into the rim rock above the river.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry chamber in the ravine wall, above the flood and below the snow.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the mechanism is the occupant.
why.pressures: The sockets are empty and the keystones are elsewhere, which is exactly the problem the type poses.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the keystones were returned, whatever the chamber does would start doing it again.

preferences: in a ravine wall, reached by a scramble

vibe.silhouette: a squared opening in a natural ravine wall
vibe.palette: white Ayleid stone, black interior, wet rock
vibe.materials: Ayleid ashlar, crystal sockets, cut channels
vibe.signatureFeature: empty keystone sockets cut so precisely that dust does not settle in them
vibe.approach: found by scrambling where there is no reason to
vibe.senses: a low resonance you feel rather than hear

places.namingRule: named for the stone worked on it
sources: lore: Lore:Argonian (jadeflint, obverdian, volcanic glass skinning shards)

why.founding: Where there is no metal there is worked stone, and the flint on this rim has been knapped on the same floor for a very long time.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry bench beside the seam, with wind to clear the dust.
why.occupantsMotive: Two or three knappers who supply four villages and the porter gangs.
why.pressures: The smithy in town has been taking their trade for twenty years.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the fastening supply held, the floor is abandoned within a generation.

preferences: upwind of the settlement it supplies

vibe.silhouette: a floor of glittering debris on a bench
vibe.palette: green-grey flint, white dust, brown rock
vibe.materials: flint, hammerstones, hide pads
vibe.signatureFeature: a debris floor half a metre deep, which is to say centuries of the same afternoon
vibe.approach: the floor glitters in low sun before you see anyone
vibe.senses: chipping; wind

places.name: The Snowline Stage
sources: lore: scour: a quarter of the interesting ground is on the rim, and it is the only ground with range; region grammar: border mountains

why.founding: The one legal crossing of the northern rim needs a staged shelter, because the pass is above the snowline for part of the year and people die on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle at 226 m: the lowest crossing of the wall for many kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who is nominally the state's and is paid by the free port, which he does not advertise.
why.pressures: The pass closes seasonally, and when it closes the ledge trade doubles.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the state funded it properly the rim would be policed and this zone's economy would change entirely.

hardConstraints: at the lowest crossing of the rim
preferences: the ledge routes within 400 m, out of its sightline

vibe.silhouette: a stone hut at the low point of a skyline notch
vibe.palette: grey stone, white above it half the year, brown below
vibe.materials: dry stone, a heavy timber roof weighted with rocks
vibe.signatureFeature: a season board that closes the pass, and a keeper who is paid by the people who profit when it does
vibe.approach: the notch is the only legible feature on the rim skyline
vibe.senses: wind; a fire that never quite warms the room

places.namingRule: named for the load rating over the pass
sources: lore: Lore:Black Marsh (Imperial roads made freight slower); Lore:Sea Transportation

why.founding: Nothing goes over the rim on a boat, so the free port's cargo is broken down here into loads a person can carry up a pass.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm ground on the river before the climb begins, with a landing and a long shed.
why.occupantsMotive: Porter gangs who hold their rate collectively and are the free port's real leverage over Morrowind.
why.pressures: Every consignment is repacked here, which means everything that goes north is known here first.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pass road were made passable to carts, the gangs lose the trade and the town loses its intelligence.

preferences: one stage from the free port
the pass within a day

vibe.silhouette: a long open shed full of carrying frames, and a landing in front of it
vibe.palette: frame timber, dust, cargo colours from four provinces
vibe.materials: frames, a rate board, weighing beams
vibe.signatureFeature: everything that crosses the rim is opened here and repacked, so the yard knows the province's cargo better than the port does
vibe.approach: the frames stacked outside read from the water
vibe.senses: counting aloud; frames knocking; a rope brake

places.namingRule: named for the emperor whose mark is on it
sources: lore: Lore:Blackrose Prison (Second Empire, raised in a day by Pelladil Direnni); Lore:Reman Empire; Lore:Akaviri

why.founding: The Second Empire cut a road-and-cistern works over this rim to move soldiers into Morrowind, and abandoned it unfinished.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle route the modern pass road still roughly follows, one contour higher.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The smugglers use its cistern for water and its cutting as shelter.
why.pressures: It is a thousand years older than anything else standing here and better built than all of it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the cistern were ever cleaned out, the rim route becomes usable in the dry season.

preferences: one contour above the modern road

vibe.silhouette: a cut ramp and a stone cistern mouth on a bare saddle
vibe.palette: grey ashlar, lichen gold, rock
vibe.materials: Akaviri-era dressed stone, a vaulted cistern, an unfinished cutting
vibe.signatureFeature: a road cutting that stops in mid-air, with the tool marks still sharp
vibe.approach: the cut line is visible against the skyline
vibe.senses: wind; water dripping into a vault

places.namingRule: named for the consignment that was lost off it
sources: lore: region grammar: border mountains; Lore:Blackwood Road (the legal crossings are few, so the illegal ones are the rim)

why.founding: A second ledge, higher and harder, used only when the north traverse is being watched.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge-end shelf at 268 m with ground falling away on three sides.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody staffs it; goods are left and collected.
why.pressures: The approach is a genuine climb and at least one consignment is still up there because the man who cached it did not come back.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port's trade were legalised, this ledge is never visited again.

preferences: higher and harder than its neighbour
goods cached, not staffed

vibe.silhouette: a shelf on a spur nose with the ground falling away on three sides
vibe.palette: bare rock, lichen, sky
vibe.materials: rock, one rotted cover, one rope
vibe.signatureFeature: a consignment nobody ever came back for, still covered, still marked
vibe.approach: a climb with no reassurance on it
vibe.senses: wind only; you are above the birds

places.name: The North Traverse
sources: lore: region grammar: border mountains; Lore:Blackwood Road (the legal crossings are few, so the illegal ones are the rim)

why.founding: The free port's cargo has to leave the province somehow, and the legal crossings into Morrowind are few — so the illegal ones are the rim itself.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench two-thirds of the way up the border wall, out of sight from below and from the pass, with a traverse line rather than a path.
why.occupantsMotive: Two or three men who move consignments and mark which side each one is going.
why.pressures: It is a four-hour climb with a load and the weather on the rim turns without warning.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pass station below were properly manned, the ledge becomes the only route and the price triples.

hardConstraints: a rim ledge out of sight of the pass
no water — this is the dry route
preferences: beside a pass, out of sight of its post
a rope left rigged

vibe.silhouette: nothing at all from below; from above, a worn traverse line across a face
vibe.palette: rock grey, and covers dyed to match it exactly
vibe.materials: rock, rope, rock-coloured canvas
vibe.signatureFeature: consignments stacked under covers dyed to the exact colour of the rock, with chalk marks saying which way each is going
vibe.approach: you are on the traverse before you know there is one
vibe.senses: wind; rope on rock; nothing human

places.namingRule: named for the order that exiled its founder
sources: lore: region grammar: border mountains; scour: the rim is the only ground with genuine sightlines

why.founding: Somebody was put out of an order and went as high as there is to go in this province, which is the northern rim.
why.siteAdvantages: Above the snowline on the border wall, with a spring that does not freeze.
why.occupantsMotive: One or two, keeping an observance nobody else keeps.
why.pressures: It is the coldest inhabited place in Argonia and reaching it is a genuine expedition.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the order that exiled them collapsed, the observance here becomes the only surviving version of it.

hardConstraints: a spring that does not freeze
preferences: the highest inhabited ground in the province

vibe.silhouette: a stone cell against a face, with snow on it — an image that exists nowhere else in this province
vibe.palette: white, rock grey, one dark doorway
vibe.materials: dry stone, a turf roof, a single ritual fitting
vibe.signatureFeature: snow, in Argonia, on an inhabited roof
vibe.approach: a full day's climb with no encouragement
vibe.senses: wind; and, extraordinarily, silence

places.namingRule: named for the province it lets you see out of
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (a quarter of the interesting ground is on the mountain rim; a view is a reward)
lore: scour finding: median site sees 18% of its 1.2 km surroundings — a view is a reward

why.founding: The rim is the one place in Argonia with a genuine long sightline, and this ledge looks back down over the whole freehold reach.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge end at 268 m with the ground falling away and no canopy.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the ground is worn where generations have stood.
why.pressures: It is the only place a traveller can actually see the shape of this zone, which makes it a navigation tool.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing changes it; that is why the smugglers use it as a lookout as well.

preferences: reveals the river reach and at least three plotted places

vibe.silhouette: a bare spur nose with nothing above it
vibe.palette: rock, lichen, and a great deal of sky
vibe.materials: worn rock, a cairn, a sighting stone
vibe.signatureFeature: the only view in the province that shows you a river system rather than a wall of trees
vibe.condition: worn smooth by four hundred years of standing
vibe.approach: you climb for an hour and the province opens
vibe.senses: wind; and the river, faintly, from very far below

places.namingRule: named for the bog it draws from
sources: lore: Lore:Black Marsh (bog iron); material-culture (metal use almost unheard of post-Duskfall)

why.founding: Somebody tried to make the freeholds self-sufficient in iron out of the bog ore, and it did not pay against stolen ship fastenings.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the ore bog with a charcoal supply and water for the bellows.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The furnace stack is intact and cold.
why.pressures: It failed commercially rather than technically, which is the more interesting failure.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the smithy's supply were cut, this is the first place anyone would come back to.

hardConstraints: ore bog and charcoal within reach
preferences: beside water for the bellows

vibe.silhouette: a clay stack the height of a man, standing alone
vibe.palette: clay ochre, slag black-green, grass
vibe.materials: clay furnace, slag heaps, charcoal pits
vibe.signatureFeature: slag heaps arranged in dated rows, which read as an argument that was slowly lost
vibe.approach: the stack looks like a termite mound until you are close
vibe.senses: nothing; wind in the slag

places.namingRule: named for the reach it works
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §2 (Alten Corimont lives on smuggling, transit and salvage)
lore: Lore:Lilmoth (the drowned quarter, salvaged for 150 years)

why.founding: The register gives the free port salvage as a named livelihood, and a river with a bar and a whitewater reach above it supplies the material.
why.siteAdvantages: On the bank below the bar, where anything lost upstream eventually grounds.
why.occupantsMotive: Divers who work the reach and dry what they bring up on frames facing the wind.
why.pressures: Their lot book records which wreck each piece came from, which is a list of every consignment lost on this river.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the reach were cleared, the yard would have to buy its stock like everyone else.

preferences: below a bar or a whitewater reach

vibe.silhouette: drying frames covered in river-blackened objects
vibe.palette: black waterlogged timber, rust, salt-white bloom
vibe.materials: frames, desalting tubs, weighted belts
vibe.signatureFeature: a lot book naming the wreck, the reach and the year for every piece on the frames
vibe.approach: the frames read from the water
vibe.senses: dripping; the river; a tub being stirred

places.name: Rockpoint
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §4 (Rockpoint, SE of Alten Corimont: Alten Corimont's rival — a competing landing that lost)
docs/quests/20-world-provisions.md §12b (the player stronghold site: one reoccupied xanmeer or abandoned river station)
lore: build-out register: player ownership needs a place shape reserved now, or it is a refactor later (0041 forward-compatibility block)

why.founding: A rival landing founded downriver to undercut Alten Corimont's list, which lost — because the river bar below it will not take a laden hull and the list will not be undercut.
why.siteAdvantages: A stone-footed landing, a warehouse shell and a defensible bank, all standing, on ground nobody now claims.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The bar that killed it also keeps casual squatters away, and Alten Corimont makes sure the story of why it failed is well told.
why.pressures: It is intact, empty, freehold ground with a river frontage — which in this zone is the most valuable unowned thing there is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If anyone repaired the landing and dredged the bar, Alten Corimont would have a competitor again, and would act.

hardConstraints: a standing landing and at least one roofed shell
downstream of the free port, below a bar
preferences: defensible bank
reserve for the Phase 30 player-stronghold study — three phase states, four allegiance re-skins

vibe.silhouette: a stone landing and a warehouse shell with no roof, standing alone on a bend
vibe.palette: grey stone, black burnt timber ends, brown river, green taking it back
vibe.materials: cut stone footings — expensive, foreign, and the reason it is still standing at all
vibe.signatureFeature: a landing built for hulls that cannot get to it, with the mooring rings still bright from a rope nobody has tied in eighty years
vibe.approach: you see the landing from the water and assume the town is behind it, and it is not
vibe.senses: river; wind through an unroofed shell; no voices at all

places.namingRule: the two banks' names, hyphenated
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (outsiders travel behind an Argonian guide)
lore: Lore:Black Marsh (outsiders arrive by ferry behind an Argonian guide)

why.founding: A free crossing kept by a village that refuses to charge, four hundred metres from a bridge that does.
why.siteAdvantages: A channel too wide to bridge cheaply and too calm to be dangerous.
why.occupantsMotive: Villagers who row anyone across for nothing, entirely to spite the span downstream.
why.pressures: The syndicate has tried three times to close it and cannot find a legal basis.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the village were bought off, the trunk road's toll becomes unavoidable.

hardConstraints: too wide or deep to ford
paired stage on the far bank
preferences: within sight of a toll crossing

vibe.silhouette: a bare stage, a boat and no toll box at all
vibe.palette: plain timber, brown water, no paint
vibe.materials: a plank stage, a pole boat, a bench
vibe.signatureFeature: a conspicuously absent toll box, with the empty bracket left up on purpose
vibe.approach: the bridge is visible from it, which is the point
vibe.senses: pole in mud; laughter aimed downstream

places.namingRule: the household's name plus 'fire'
sources: lore: Lore:Argonian (a comer cannot be refused); pacing: a hostile province needs a safety floor outside its cities

why.founding: Even in a zone that prices everything, the obligation not to refuse a comer holds — and the household that keeps it is quietly the most respected thing on the trunk.
why.siteAdvantages: On the trunk at a day's travel from the next fire, on ground that never floods.
why.occupantsMotive: One household, four generations, one fire.
why.pressures: They give away what the tradehouse two hours on sells, and neither side mentions it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If they ever charged, the zone would lose the one thing it has that is not for sale.

hardConstraints: fire visible from the road at night
preferences: a day's travel from the next hearth house

vibe.silhouette: one lit doorway and a fire, deliberately visible from the road
vibe.palette: fire orange in a grey landscape, thatch, smoke
vibe.materials: mud render, thatch, one enormous hearth
vibe.signatureFeature: a guest tally on the doorframe that includes names the port list would like to have
vibe.mood: the safest place in a zone with no law
vibe.approach: the fire is the cue, at the hour you need it
vibe.senses: fire; cooking; somebody already awake

places.namingRule: named for the mile-mark it stands at
sources: lore: Morrowind's corner club / tradehouse pattern (morrowind-content-density.md); Lore:Hissmir Fish-Eye Rye

why.founding: A day's travel out on the northern trunk, which is exactly where a paid bed sells to people who cannot reach the port before dark.
why.siteAdvantages: A ford with firm ground, a landing and space for beasts.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who takes coin, barter and — reluctantly — obligation.
why.pressures: It is the last place before the rim where a stranger is served without questions.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the trunk were rerouted the house is worthless within a year.

hardConstraints: on the trunk at day-travel spacing
preferences: last service before the rim

vibe.silhouette: a long low building with lamps at a road bend
vibe.palette: whitewash, thatch, lamp yellow
vibe.materials: timber frame, thatch, a stone-flagged main room
vibe.signatureFeature: three price columns chalked at the door: coin, goods, and owed
vibe.approach: lamps at the bend, in a landscape with none
vibe.senses: beasts; kitchen; travellers comparing routes

places.name: The Trunk Span
sources: world/sources/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md (every crossing in the province has an owner)
lore: labour-and-bondage dossier (every crossing has an owner); Lore:Keel-Sakka (the Tum-Taleel's bridge)

why.founding: The northern trunk road crosses the river at its narrowest point, and the crossing has an owner — as every crossing here does.
why.siteAdvantages: A water narrows with hard banks, on the Stormhold-to-Thorn line.
why.occupantsMotive: Four toll-takers working for a freehold syndicate that bought the span outright.
why.pressures: The Owing operates at this crossing, as it does at every tolled crossing in the route graph, and the ledger is kept in the open.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port bought the span, Stormhold's road trade would be paying Alten Corimont directly, which is why it has not happened.

hardConstraints: spans the channel at its narrowest
preferences: a free ford 200-400 m off that the locals use
the owner lives within sight

vibe.silhouette: a plank span with a barrier and a hut at one end
vibe.palette: plank grey, tariff board white, brown water
vibe.materials: planked timber on driven piles, a rope barrier
vibe.signatureFeature: a tariff board that prices people, goods and obligation in three separate columns
vibe.approach: the barrier is visible from a long way along a straight road
vibe.senses: planks under feet; a bored voice quoting a rate

places.namingRule: named for the syndicate that owns it
sources: lore: labour-and-bondage dossier (every crossing has an owner); Lore:Keel-Sakka (the Tum-Taleel's bridge)

why.founding: An old stone arch upriver that two freehold syndicates both claim, because the deed was written before either existed.
why.siteAdvantages: The only stone crossing in the zone, at a ravine pinch.
why.occupantsMotive: Two sets of toll-takers, on alternate weeks, by an arrangement that is not holding.
why.pressures: Travellers are charged twice as often as they are charged once.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either syndicate forced the issue there would be blood on a bridge that nobody wants damaged.

hardConstraints: a stone span at a ravine pinch
preferences: two rival toll huts, one at each end

vibe.silhouette: a stone arch with a hut at each end, and two different tariff boards
vibe.palette: grey stone, two different paint colours applied competitively
vibe.materials: dressed stone — the only stone crossing here
vibe.signatureFeature: two tariff boards on the same bridge, each defacing the other
vibe.condition: the bridge is immaculate and the huts are not
vibe.approach: you can see both huts before you commit to the span
vibe.senses: two arguments, one either side

places.namingRule: named for its last legitimate consignment
sources: lore: guilds-and-orders dossier (the EEC is gone; its wharves and bonded stores are not)

why.founding: A second Company store upriver at the head of navigation, too far from anywhere to be worth defending.
why.siteAdvantages: On the old wharf above the transfer stages.
why.occupantsMotive: A family living in one corner of a hall built for two hundred tons.
why.pressures: The sealed section at the back has never been opened and the family keeps it that way, superstitiously.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the sealed section were opened, the family loses the only reason anyone respects them.

preferences: at the head of navigation

vibe.palette: grey stone, one small warm window
vibe.materials: Imperial stone, later partitions of crate timber
vibe.signatureFeature: a household living in one lit corner of an enormous dark hall
vibe.approach: the single window in a huge blank wall
vibe.senses: echo; a family's small noises made large

places.namingRule: named for the campaign its founders fought
sources: lore: Lore:Accession War; Lore:Argonian Invasion of Morrowind (4E 5-6); Lore:Tear

why.founding: Argonians who went north into Morrowind in the 4E came back and would not settle in ordinary villages, so they made their own holding on the border they had crossed.
why.siteAdvantages: High firm ground with a view of the pass, chosen for the sightline rather than the soil.
why.occupantsMotive: Veterans and their children, armed, organised, and not answerable to the free port.
why.pressures: They are the only armed force in the zone and everyone is careful about what they are asked to do.
why.wouldChangeIf: If they were ever hired by the port, the freeholds become a power rather than a market.

hardConstraints: a view of the border crossing
preferences: deliberately apart from the free port
